title: retrieval-stress-casebook-8k-32k-128k
content:
Purpose and scope:
This note is a compact casebook for our long-context + retrieval stress experiments across 8k, 32k, and 128k context lengths. The goal: characterize failure modes (truncation, attention sink behavior, retrieval contamination), produce a small prompt set for regression monitoring, and recommend mitigations for onboarding new model variants into production routing.

Audience:
Applied ML engs, model onboarding owners, SREs responsible for runtime kernel behavior, and product owners monitoring quality regressions.

High-level summary (TL;DR):
- 8k baseline: stable for our canonical prompts, truncation rare when retrieval payload <50% of context.
- 32k: visible degradation when retrieval sets include many short documents (high doc-count), leading to attention-sink triggers and hallucination spikes in the reranking task.
- 128k: worst-case failure surface is dominated by KV-cache pressure and token-dropping during batching spikes; truncation occurs unpredictably if prefix caching isn't honored.
- Actionables: add three small checks to onboarding pipeline (prefix-preservation test, per-doc-length sensitivity, and eviction-resilience check) and a 32k-focused reranking prompt set for regression alerts.

Experimental setup (notes + reproducible-ish):
- Models tested: new-onboard-cand-v1, baseline-serving-v3 (control).
- Hardware: dedicated A100 80GB and a mixed NVLink pool (to surface memory fragmentation).
- Serving runtime: continuous-batching enabled, prefix/KV cache enabled for all tests.
- Retrieval simulator: we use a synthetic retriever to vary (a) doc_count, (b) avg_doc_length, (c) insert_positions (prefix vs suffix).
- Metrics collected: truncation_rate (requests with >0 token loss compared to expected), attention_sink_incidents (counts of early attention collapse events flagged by model logits diagnostics), rerank_AP@10, generation_levenshtein (on deterministic gold answers), p50/p95 latency, mean_tokens_per_request, memory_eviction_events.

Test matrix (representative grid):
- Context lengths: 8k, 32k, 128k
- Retrieval payload profiles: small-few (10 docs × 200 tokens), large-many (200 docs × 200 tokens), many-short (200 docs × 50 tokens), single-long (1 doc × 60k tokens for 128k runs)
- Insert position: prefix (retrieved docs appended before prompt), suffix (after prompt), interleaved (chunks interleaved between prompt sections)
- Concurrency: 1, 8, 32 concurrent streams (to trigger batching behavior)

Representative prompts (included in regression harness):
1) "Contextual QA (fact-recall)" - short user question with retrieval prefix of 20-200 docs. Expectation: exact answer span in top-1 generation.
Example prompt snippet:
"<RETRIEVED_DOCS>\nUser: What is the licensing requirement mentioned for dataset X in the 3rd paragraph?\nAssistant:"

2) "Multi-hop policy synthesis" - long instructions + interleaved retrieval pieces. Expectation: structured step list; catch hallucination and attention drift.
3) "Rerank test" - candidate list of 50 retrieval snippets; metric: AP@10 for relevance labels.
4) "Instruction-with-long-appendix" - user asks to summarize a 40k-token appendix. Expectation: concise 6-8 bullet summary.

Key findings (observations and hypotheses):
- Truncation patterns:
  - 8k: truncation_rate <1% for small-few and many-short. Causes when seen: unexpected headers in retrieval docs (very long HTML-style boilerplate) pushing the usable prompt over limit.
  - 32k: truncation spikes when many-short profile combined with concurrent batching. Hypothesis: continuous batching merges request token counts but runtime classifies combined sequence incorrectly for per-request truncation heuristics (bug suspected in per-request seqlength calculation after KV attach).
  - 128k: Not consistent — sometimes the first 4k tokens of the prompt are preserved and later chunks are dropped (non-monotonic trimming). Indicates possible race condition in cache population and request splice ordering under heavy KV pressure.

- Attention-sink triggers:
  - Symptoms: model outputs long repeated phrase segments or abrupt derailment to a high-frequency token. Logits diagnostics show a sudden collapse in attention weights beyond a certain step (typically after consuming ~20–30k prompt tokens).
  - Correlation: high doc_count and many-short profile correlate with increased incidence. Also correlated with memory evictions on A100 (suggests kernel/regenerator path fallback causes transient numerical instability).

- Retrieval contamination (source leakage):
  - When retrieved docs contain similar question framing, model sometimes surfaces boilerplate rather than synthesized answers (over-reliance on exact matches). More common in 32k and 128k when many doc boundaries exist — attention focuses on earliest matching token rather than reasoning over synthesized content.

Quantitative snapshot (sample numbers from runs on new-onboard-cand-v1):
- 8k, small-few, concurrency=1: truncation_rate=0.6%, rerank_AP@10=0.86, p95 latency=210ms
- 32k, many-short, concurrency=8: truncation_rate=4.2%, attention_sink_incidents=18/1000 requests, rerank_AP@10=0.72, p95 latency=480ms
- 128k, single-long, concurrency=1: truncation_rate=2.8% (non-monotonic), attention_sink_incidents=5/200 requests, rerank_AP@10=0.69, p95 latency=1.2s
- Memory_eviction_events higher on mixed NVLink pool for 32k/128k runs vs A100 pool (by ~3x).

Failure case examples (from log snippets):
- "... <DOC_37> ... User: summarize. Assistant: " then repeat of "Summary:" token 200+ times — attention-sink-like.
- "Prefix preserved\n<Request id: abc123> expected tokens 32000, served 31456" — truncation occurred but logs show per-request accounting as 32000; discrepancy suggests post-augmentation trimming.

Immediate diagnostics to run before onboarding approval:
- Prefix-preservation test: feed request with retrieval prefix tagged; assert prefix tokens present verbatim in first N tokens. If not, fail onboarding.
- Per-doc-length sensitivity: sweep avg_doc_length from 25→2k tokens and measure rerank_AP@10 and truncation_rate; flag model variants with >2x degradation vs baseline in any bucket.
- Eviction-resilience test: synthetic memory pressure injected during request streaming; measure attention_sink_incidents.

Mitigations and runtime-workarounds:
- Short-term (serving layer): enforce per-request hard-limits before continuous-batching merge (i.e., compute and persist per-request expected_seq_len into batch scheduling). Patch in review: github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/452
- Mid-term: implement a prefix-anchoring mechanism that marks retrieval tokens as non-evictable during initial KV population window. Requires kernel-side pointer support.
- Prompt engineering: for many-short retrievals, condense documents via a light-weight summarizer before attaching to prompt (cheap transformer micromodel or heuristic truncation preserving first N sentences).

Regression harness additions (practical checklist):
- Add the above representative prompts to nightly onboarding-run corpus.
- New metrics to publish: attention_sink_rate (counts per 10k requests), truncation_discrepancy_rate (mismatch between expected_len and actual served), per-doc-boundary_hallucination_score (heuristic: matches to retrieved text >70% ratio flagged).
- Alert thresholds: attention_sink_rate >5/1000 triggers P1; truncation_discrepancy_rate >1% triggers onboarding block.

Open questions / unknowns:
- Is the non-monotonic token dropping reproducible deterministically or only under noisy concurrency? We need a minimal reproducible test case (preferably on A100 single-tenant hardware).
- Are attention-sink incidents more numerical-instability than data/architecture? Need logits precision trace (float16->float32 fallback detection).

Next steps (owners and timeline):
- Diego: implement prefix-preservation quick-check endpoint and add to onboarding CI (ETA 2 weeks).
- Fiona: extend rerank AP test to include many-short profile with labels from existing eval set (ETA 1 week).
- Jamal: run isolated 128k single-tenant reproducibility experiments and capture full logits/time-series for 20 failure cases (ETA 3 weeks).
- Product/Release: hold onboarding for new-onboard-cand-v1 until prefix-preservation check passes and attention_sink_rate <= baseline + 20% in regression harness.

Notes to reviewers (informal):
- This doc intentionally mixes concrete numbers from a single test campaign and heuristics; treat the numbers as indicative, not canonical.
- Feel free to paste the prompt snippets above into the harness and iterate — the many-short profile is particularly fragile and worth instrumenting early.

TODOs / loose ends:
- Collect example request ids for all reported attention_sink_incidents and attach to a follow-up doc (file size will be large).
- Add example golden outputs for the instruction-with-long-appendix prompt (helps automated diff in regression runs).

Acknowledgements and references:
- Thanks to infra (SRE) for providing mixed NVLink pool for debugging.
- See linked artifacts for the infra PR and Jira ticket tracking the per-request accounting bug.

End of note.
